name: mating-draft-clearance
source: mcweed I-7 / U533-U541 (pin shoulder and wedge flare vs the finger inner edge) and mined4 'sweep tests (motion)': a fit that is checked at the pose the parts start in, never at the pose they reach. Same class as I-6 (mined2), where the constraint sentence -- 'strictly shorter than the interior, below the keyways' -- was what finally pinned the geometry.
summary: A 6 degree drafted plug and its socket. The stated clearance is 0.2 PERPENDICULAR to the drafted face, which is a horizontal offset of 0.2/cos(6) = 0.2011 -- worth only 0.001 mm, and not the trap. The trap is the pocket depth: parallel tapered walls mean the plug does not stop at the flush pose, it sinks clearPerp/sin(6) = 1.913 mm past flush before all four gaps close at once. The floor has to clear the nose by 0.5 at THAT pose, so the pocket is 12 + 1.913 + 0.5 = 14.413 deep. The natural answer, 12 + 0.5 = 12.5, renders correctly, passes a static check at the flush pose, and is 1.9 mm too shallow -- the nose bottoms out before the wedge grabs. Note for authors: the perpendicular-vs-horizontal reading on its own is NOT discriminable at any sane draft angle (0.2*(1/cos(15)-1) is still only 0.007 mm), so the asfailed makes both mistakes and only the depth one is measurable.
